questions.question: State three rules for resistors connected in series.
questions.expected_answer: The current is the same at every point; the source voltage divides between the resistors, and their voltages add up to the source voltage; adding resistors increases the total resistance, so the current decreases.

questions.question: Two identical bulbs are connected in series to a 6 V battery. State the voltage across each bulb and explain what happens to the current and brightness if a third identical bulb is added.
questions.expected_answer: Each has 3 V (3 + 3 = 6 V). Adding a third bulb increases the total resistance, so the current decreases; each bulb then has 2 V and all three glow more dimly.

questions.question: Explain why all the bulbs go out if one bulb in a series circuit is removed.
questions.expected_answer: A series circuit has only one path. Removing a bulb breaks that path, so the circuit is open and no current can flow anywhere.
